analysis: The only production change is in SSDBlockStore.readExactly (head lines 479-505). It removes the up-front reserveCapacity(count) and adds a fast path: when the first read returns exactly `count` bytes with startIndex == 0, that buffer is returned without copying. Otherwise it reserves capacity once and appends as before. The size bound is unchanged. Callers (readHeader) still cap wrappedLen and metadataLen at min(maxHeaderFieldBytes, caller maximum) before readExactly, so the unauthenticated-length allocation limit in T-041 is preserved. If anything, deferring reserveCapacity reduces allocation for short or truncated files. The beforeRead charging sequence is unchanged (count first, then 0 per loop iteration), which the new test pins. Return semantics are the same: exactly `count` bytes, or a truncated error on EOF. I found no change to AES-GCM, AAD, HKDF nonce derivation, the metadata fields or canonical JSON, path safety (isSafeBlockURL, no-follow open), the temp sweep, or the HMAC lookup tags. The T-041 posture (HMAC names, 30-minute TTL, KEK purge, no prompt-derived plaintext metadata) is therefore unaffected. A Data slice returned uncopied could share a backing buffer, but the startIndex == 0 check guards callers that index from zero. readHeader uses subdata/prefix and the metadata decoder, which are unaffected by sharing. The test file change only adds a short-read unit test using a temp fixture and has no production effect. Remaining uncertainty: I did not see the other readExactly callers in readStreaming or SSDBlockChunkCursor. They live outside the supplied units, and I assume they follow the same zero-index usage and keep their own length bounds.
